subject.title: [Bug]: gateway.nodes.denyCommands silently accepts invalid command names without warning

question: Should `gateway.nodes.denyCommands` config writes warn and continue, fail closed, or stay audit-only when entries are unknown or pattern-like and plugin/custom command IDs may exist?
rationale: The source-level gap is clear, but the security contract is a human choice because fail-closed validation improves typo safety while warning-only behavior avoids blocking valid plugin or future node command IDs.

options.title: Warn and continue
options.body: Emit write-time warnings for unknown or pattern-like deny entries using the audit vocabulary, but keep the write valid so plugin/custom command IDs are not blocked.

options.title: Fail closed
options.body: Reject unknown or pattern-like deny entries at config write time, accepting compatibility risk unless a plugin-aware exemption is designed first.

options.title: Stay audit-only
options.body: Keep config writes permissive and rely on `openclaw security audit` to report ineffective deny entries after the fact.

recommendation.title: Warn and continue
recommendation.body: Emit write-time warnings for unknown or pattern-like deny entries using the audit vocabulary, but keep the write valid so plugin/custom command IDs are not blocked.

likelyOwner.reason: This choice affects security posture and Gateway command-policy semantics, and recent history points to adjacent denyCommands/security policy work.
